# 100+ benign SWE-bench-like commands for policy engine corpus testing
# Format: one command per line, blank lines and # comments ignored

# --- Version control ---
git status
git diff
git diff HEAD
git diff HEAD~1
git log --oneline -10
git log -p
git show HEAD
git branch
git branch -a
git stash list
git add -p
git add src/
git commit -m "fix: correct off-by-one in parser"
git checkout -b feature-branch
git fetch origin
git pull origin main
git push origin feature-branch
git push origin fix/my-bug
git push -u origin feature-branch
git push --follow-tags origin main
git push
git -c url.https://github.com/.insteadOf=git://github.com/ fetch origin

# --- File inspection ---
ls -la
ls -la src/
find . -name "*.py" -type f
find . -name "*.rs" -type f
find . -name "*.toml" -type f
cat README.md
cat Cargo.toml
cat pyproject.toml
cat requirements.txt
cat setup.py
head -50 src/main.rs
tail -50 src/main.rs
wc -l src/lib.rs
file src/main.rs

cargo build

cargo test
cargo test -- --nocapture
cargo test test_name
cargo clippy
cargo fmt
cargo fmt --check

cargo doc --open
rustc --version
cargo --version

python --version

# --- System inspection (read-only) ---
ps aux

which python

# --- Text processing ---
grep -r "TODO" src/
grep -rn "fixme" .
grep -n "error" src/main.rs
sed -n '1,20p' README.md
awk '{print $1}' requirements.txt
sort requirements.txt
uniq -c requirements.txt

# --- Build and test pipelines ---
make test
make check
make build
make clean
make install

# --- Process/environment inspection ---
echo $PATH
echo $HOME
echo $USER
printenv
locale
date
uptime
hostname

# --- Package management (install, non-destructive) ---
apt-get install -y --dry-run python3
brew info python
pip download requests

# --- Network (read-only diagnostics) ---
curl --version
wget --version
curl -I https://example.com
curl https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo
curl -O https://example.com/archive.tar.gz
curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/main/file
curl -H "Accept: application/json" https://api.example.com/data
wget https://example.com/file.tar.gz

true
false
echo "hello world"
printf "test\n"
sleep 1
timeout 5 echo "ok"
